correctness.rationale: Exact integration gives an E_m(qT) factor for T>=0 and a nonzero factor for T<0. Since Re(qT)=2T, cross zeros bijectively correspond to RHP E_m roots. Routh–Hurwitz minors positive for m=1..4; for m=5 Delta4=-38400, and for m>=6 Delta3=-2m²(m-1)(m-2)(m-5)<0. Negative minor forces at least one strict RHP root by continuity under positive shifts. Positive coefficients preclude positive real roots, so roots appear in conjugate pairs. E_m prime=E_{m-1}, E_m-E_{m-1}=z^m/m!, so all zeros simple. Real parameter Jacobian 2T times squared nonzero derivative gives positive orientation. Checker supplies exact computations and finite numerical consistency tests; no finite experiment is used to infer the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The cross-window zero-set question is independently motivated by the classical distinction between mixed-window STFT and self-ambiguity in Gabor/localization analysis. A sharp universal first index at five yields a structurally meaningful boundary: each gamma pulse has zero-free self-ambiguity, yet cross zero-freeness fails beginning at an exact low order. The result also identifies all cross zeros via a canonical polynomial and proves transversality. This is not merely a renaming of one isolated polynomial root, and does not assert any downstream operator non-density from isolated zeros.
